description: Frederick Douglass, born into slavery in Talbot County, Maryland, tells his own story in eleven short chapters: separated from his mother, passed between masters, taught the alphabet by a mistress and then forbidden more. Published in Boston in 1845, seven years after he reached the North, it set out what slavery did to enslaved people and to the people who held them, in plain, controlled prose. Douglass signed it with his own name, at a time when that was not safe.

title: The Red Badge of Courage
author: Stephen Crane
description: Henry Fleming, called “the youth,” is a Union private who has dreamed of glory and now waits for his regiment’s first battle, unsure how he will behave when it comes. Crane follows him in close third person through noise, smoke, rumour and the talk of the men around him. Stephen Crane wrote it in 1893–94, before he had ever been in combat, and Appleton published it in New York in 1895.

title: Bliss, and Other Stories
author: Katherine Mansfield
description: Katherine Mansfield’s 1920 collection gathers fourteen stories, from “Prelude”, a Wellington family’s move to a new house, to “Bliss”, in which a woman’s radiant mood at her own dinner party meets an unwelcome discovery. Mansfield, born in New Zealand, was already ill with tuberculosis when she assembled it.

title: The Garden Party, and Other Stories
author: Katherine Mansfield
description: Katherine Mansfield’s 1922 collection gathers fifteen stories, opening with “At the Bay”, a summer day at a New Zealand seaside, and “The Garden Party”, in which a family’s party goes ahead after a neighbour’s death. Mansfield wrote several of them in Switzerland while ill with tuberculosis, and died the following January.

title: Dubliners
author: James Joyce
description: James Joyce’s Dubliners (1914) gathers fifteen stories of middle-class Dublin life, arranged from childhood through adolescence and maturity to public life. It opens with a boy and a dead priest in “The Sisters”, passes through the bazaar of “Araby”, and ends with a Christmastime party and a wife’s memory in “The Dead”. Joyce wrote the stories between 1904 and 1907, and the book took until 1914 to find a publisher.

title: Mrs. Dalloway
author: Virginia Woolf
description: Virginia Woolf’s Mrs Dalloway (1925) follows a single day in the life of Clarissa Dalloway, a wealthy woman in post-First World War London, from her morning errands to the party she gives that evening. Woolf began it as a short story, “Mrs Dalloway in Bond Street”, and its working title was The Hours.

title: La Mare au Diable
author: George Sand
description: George Sand’s La Mare au Diable (The Devil’s Pool, 1846) is the first of her four pastoral novels. Germain, a twenty-eight-year-old widower with three children, is urged by his father-in-law to remarry and sets off to meet a well-off widow, taking a sixteen-year-old girl, Marie, who is going to a new job. A night by the pond of the title changes what he wants. Sand says it grew from a Holbein engraving of a ploughman and a scene she watched at sowing time.
